source.title: Simpler Certified Radius Maximization by Propagating Covariances
source.authors: Xing-Jian Zhen; Rudrasis Chakraborty; Vikas Singh

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix; some figure and table extraction is flattened, but the relevant tabular values remain identifiable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and certified-robustness results, but they do not measure whether gradient-trained networks reach near-zero training classification error or test any listed version. Its accuracy and certified-radius comparisons do not establish training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper trains robust classifiers and evaluates test accuracy, certified accuracy/radius, training speed, noisy-label test accuracy, and covariance estimates. These are not training classification error results of the kind named in V1–V6. Its statements about removing batch normalization and replacing max pooling describe the proposed recipe, not a test of the listed normalization or shortcut claims.
record.test_reason: The study measures certified robustness, test accuracy, covariance-estimation quality, and the runtime of its proposed training method. None measures a listed claim version. Removing batch normalization and using residual architectures supplies no controlled test of normalization, shortcuts, or optimization with depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: approximate covariance propagation enables efficient certified-radius maximization with competitive robustness and faster training at moderate depth, with some performance compromise. The authors also describe noisy-label training as promising.
record.recipe_differences: A covariance-propagation method for certified-radius robust training; it does not test the original training-error claim or a listed version.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that estimates become looser as networks grow deeper and that performance depends on perturbation size; Places365 ablations also vary λ and rmax.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 and Figure 5 report up to 5× faster training than MACER on CIFAR-10 and 1.5× on larger datasets, with competitive certified robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate covariance propagation reduces the computational cost of certified-radius maximization.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 and appendix Table b report test accuracy of 0.808 on CIFAR-10 and 0.346 on CIFAR-100 under 45% pair-flipping label noise; neither reports training classification error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed method achieves these test accuracies when trained with corrupted labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 and appendix G report looser covariance bounds in deeper networks. These are approximation errors rather than training-error degradation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The quality of covariance upper bounds deteriorates with network depth.

record.problems: The supplied text gives no training classification-error results. Several comparisons are presented in figures without exact numeric values, and the method's covariance estimates become looser with depth and larger perturbations.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted because none of the reported outcomes measures the behavior named by V1–V6. The paper's numeric results concern certified robustness, test accuracy, speed, and covariance estimates.

untested.parts: Training classification error on clean or corrupted labels and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization-based alternatives.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization, including the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's relation from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. No result rows or version verdicts are warranted. The runtime comparisons do not isolate batch normalization, and successful training without normalization does not establish the speed or stability comparisons specified by V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels as a training-error test, and model-size effects.
Teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error, depth effects, and training without normalization.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature, and loss dynamics above the stability limit.
Training-speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons attributable to batch normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
